hero_kpi_rationale: Digital sales represent a structural shift in customer behavior and are a key driver of convenience, loyalty, and margin efficiency in Chipotle's modernized business model. At 36.7% of revenue, this reflects strong adoption of digital ordering and integration with the Rewards program.

kpis.name: Digital Sales Mix
kpis.explanation: Percentage of sales made through digital platforms (app, website).
kpis.description: Digital sales represent more than one-third of total sales, highlighting the effectiveness of technology investments and the Rewards program.
kpis.signal: Strong customer engagement via digital channels

kpis.name: Total Revenue
kpis.explanation: Total revenue generated from restaurant sales and delivery.
kpis.description: Revenue is growing due to new restaurants and pricing power, despite a decline in in-store transactions.

kpis.name: Comparable Sales
kpis.explanation: Change in revenue for restaurants open for more than one year.
kpis.description: Comparable sales declined 1.7% in 2025, primarily due to a drop in transactions (2.9%), partially offset by an increase in average check size (1.2%).

kpis.name: New Restaurants Opened
kpis.explanation: Number of company-operated new restaurants opened during the year.
kpis.description: Opening 334 new restaurants in 2025 demonstrates a high expansion pace, with 257 equipped with Chipotlane to optimize pickup efficiency.

kpis.name: Gross Margin
kpis.explanation: Percentage of revenue after deducting cost of food, beverage, and packaging (100% - FBP %).
kpis.description: Gross margin improved slightly to 70.4%, driven by efficiency gains and price increases, despite inflation in beef and chicken.

kpis.name: Labor Cost (% of Revenue)
kpis.explanation: Labor expenses as a percentage of total revenue.
kpis.description: Labor cost increased to 25.1% of revenue due to wage inflation and lower sales volumes. MD&A notes this reflects 0.7% impact from lower sales volumes and 0.4% from wage inflation.

kpis.name: Occupancy Costs (% of Revenue)
kpis.explanation: Costs related to rent and restaurant occupancy, expressed as a percentage of revenue.
kpis.description: Occupancy costs increased slightly due to new restaurant openings and lower sales, partially offset by price increases.

kpis.name: Other Operating Costs (% of Revenue)
kpis.explanation: Operating expenses excluding labor, rent, and cost of goods sold (marketing, energy, etc.).
kpis.description: Increased to 14.7%, primarily due to 0.5% from marketing and promotional activities, 0.2% from lower sales volumes, and 0.2% from natural gas and electricity inflation.
kpis.signal: Energy inflation and increased marketing spend

kpis.name: Percentage of New Restaurants with Chipotlane
kpis.explanation: Percentage of new restaurants opened with a dedicated pickup lane (Chipotlane).
kpis.description: In 2025, 257 of 334 new restaurants (77.0%) were equipped with Chipotlane. For 2026, approximately 80% of new restaurants are expected to include Chipotlane, enhancing pickup efficiency and digital sales.

kpis.name: Partner Restaurants Opened
kpis.explanation: Number of new restaurants opened by international partners.
kpis.description: 11 new partner restaurants opened in 2025, primarily in the Middle East, marking acceleration in international strategy (vs 3 in 2024).

risks.title: Decline in Comparable Sales
risks.score_rationale: The risk factor is mentioned in the Sales Trends and Results of Operations sections. The language is clear and concerning: 'Comparable restaurant sales decreased 1.7%'. This negative growth contrasts with a 7.4% increase in 2024, indicating deterioration. The Industrial category is moderately weighted.

risks.title: Labor Cost Pressure
risks.score_rationale: The factor is detailed in Labor Costs with a 0.4 percentage point increase as a percentage of revenue. The text cites 'restaurant wage inflation' as a major cause. The language is factual but concerning, especially combined with lower volumes. Same trend as prior year, but intensified.

risks.title: Impact of Tariffs on Costs
risks.score_rationale: Mentioned in Food, Beverage and Packaging Costs: '0.2% impact from tariffs enacted in 2025'. The language is measured, but uncertainty around 'future tariff policy changes' adds recurring risk. The Macro category is heavily weighted.

risks.title: Rising Operating Costs
risks.score_rationale: Other Operating Costs increased by 0.8 percentage points as a percentage of revenue. The text cites 'higher marketing and promotional activities' and 'inflation in natural gas and electricity'. The tone is neutral but figures are significant. Risk recurring across multiple line items.

risks.title: Dependence on Digital Sales
risks.score_rationale: Digital sales represent 36.7% of revenue. While not explicitly presented as a risk, the high share indicates vulnerability to technical outages or platform changes. Not directly mentioned, but implied in the KPIs. The Technology category is less weighted.

risks.title: Lease and Rental Obligation Risk
risks.score_rationale: The contractual obligations table shows $8.3 billion in future lease payments. Mentioned in Liquidity and Capital Resources. The amount is substantial, and the text includes 'reasonably certain renewal periods', increasing commitment. Language is cautious but data is significant.

risks.title: International Expansion Slowdown
risks.score_rationale: Only 14 partner restaurants internationally, with 11 in the Middle East. Development is slow and concentrated in a volatile region. Not explicitly a risk, but limited and risky geographic exposure is implicit. The Geopolitical category is moderately weighted.
